framework: AWS WAF Best Practices + PCI DSS v4.0 Mapping
description: Checklist for assessing AWS WAF posture (WAFv2 and legacy WAF Classic), including logging, coverage, and rule effectiveness.

items.title: Internet-facing ALBs should be protected by AWS WAF
items.description: Internet-facing Application Load Balancers without an associated WAF Web ACL increase exposure to common web attacks. For PCI DSS in-scope public-facing web apps, a WAF is required.
items.remediation: Associate a WAFv2 Web ACL to each internet-facing ALB hosting public applications. Start with AWS Managed Rules (CommonRuleSet, SQLi) and add rate-based rules.

pci_dss.reason: Public-facing web applications must be protected by an automated technical solution that detects and prevents web-based attacks (e.g., WAF).

items.title: CloudFront distributions serving public applications should be protected by AWS WAF
items.description: CloudFront distributions with no WebACL association are not protected by AWS WAF at the edge.
items.remediation: Create/associate a WAFv2 Web ACL (Scope=CLOUDFRONT) to CloudFront distributions for public applications. Enable AWS Managed Rules and tune false positives using Count mode before enforcing Block.

pci_dss.reason: A WAF in front of public-facing web applications is a direct requirement of PCI DSS v4.0.

items.title: WAFv2 Web ACL logging should be enabled
items.description: Without WAF logging, attack investigation, tuning, and forensic review are limited. Logging should be enabled to an approved destination (Kinesis Firehose, S3, CloudWatch Logs).
items.remediation: Enable WAF logging for each Web ACL. Configure secure destinations and retention (e.g., S3 with object lock/lifecycle).

pci_dss.reason: Audit logs must be enabled and active. WAF logs are a security-relevant log source for web attack detection and response.
Logs must include sufficient detail and be protected. Centralized WAF logging supports completeness and integrity.

items.title: WAF logs should redact sensitive request components
items.description: WAF logs may include sensitive data (e.g., Authorization headers, cookies, query strings). Redaction reduces risk of logging secrets or PAN-related data.
items.remediation: Configure WAF log redaction for sensitive headers and fields (Authorization, Cookie, X-Api-Key, etc.). Review application-specific sensitive parameters.

pci_dss.reason: Sensitive authentication data must not be stored after authorization. Redacting sensitive data from logs supports preventing storage in log streams.
Audit logs must be secured and limited to what is necessary. Redaction reduces exposure in audit trails.

items.title: WAF Web ACLs should have visibility metrics enabled
items.description: VisibilityConfig should enable CloudWatch metrics and sampled requests to support tuning and incident response.
items.remediation: Enable CloudWatch metrics and sampled requests for Web ACLs and critical rules. Use metrics to identify noisy rules and tune.

pci_dss.reason: Monitoring and alerting requires telemetry. Visibility metrics enable detection and response workflows.

items.title: WAF Web ACLs should include AWS Managed Rules for common threats
items.description: Web ACLs without baseline managed rules are typically ineffective against common web vulnerabilities (OWASP Top 10 classes).
items.remediation: Add AWS Managed Rules such as CommonRuleSet, SQLiRuleSet, KnownBadInputs, AmazonIpReputationList. Validate with Count mode then enforce Block.

pci_dss.reason: Security controls should address common software attacks. Managed rules provide standardized protection against known web attack patterns.
A WAF solution must be configured to detect and prevent attacks; managed rules are a baseline configuration capability.

items.title: WAF rules should not remain in Count-only mode for production protection
items.description: Count actions are useful for tuning, but leaving critical protections permanently in Count-only mode reduces actual prevention effectiveness.
items.remediation: After tuning and validating false positives, switch key rules from Count to Block/Challenge/Captcha. Document exceptions.

pci_dss.reason: The control requires prevention (not only detection). Count-only rules may not prevent web-based attacks.

items.title: Rate-based rules should be used to mitigate abuse and L7 DoS
items.description: Rate-based rules help mitigate brute force, credential stuffing, scraping, and L7 DoS patterns.
items.remediation: Add rate-based rules (per-IP or custom keys). Start with conservative limits and tune using metrics and sampled requests.

pci_dss.reason: Organizations must be able to respond to and manage DoS attacks. Rate-based protections are preventative controls supporting this requirement.

items.title: IP sets should not include overly broad ranges (0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0)
items.description: Overly broad IP allow/deny sets can accidentally allowlist the entire internet or block legitimate traffic unpredictably.
items.remediation: Review IP sets for broad ranges. Replace with specific CIDRs. Use separate allowlists for admin portals and ensure change control for modifications.

pci_dss.reason: Access to system components should be restricted. Overly broad allowlists undermine network-level and application-level access restrictions.

items.title: WAF Classic should be migrated to WAFv2
items.description: WAF Classic is legacy and lacks modern capabilities and consistent APIs. Migrating to WAFv2 improves control quality and maintainability.
items.remediation: Plan migration of Classic Web ACLs to WAFv2. Validate behavior using Count mode and staged deployment. Remove legacy ACLs after cutover.

pci_dss.reason: Secure configurations should follow industry-accepted standards. Using legacy/obsolete security controls can create gaps in hardening and monitoring.

items.title: Unused or unassociated Web ACLs should be reviewed
items.description: Unassociated Web ACLs indicate configuration drift and reduce audit clarity.
items.remediation: Review unassociated Web ACLs. Delete unused ACLs or document intended future use. Ensure naming and tagging standards.

pci_dss.reason: Maintaining an accurate inventory of in-scope components includes security controls and their scope/associations.

items.title: WAF rule group reuse should be standardized
items.description: Standardized reusable rule groups reduce configuration drift and support consistent protection across applications.
items.remediation: Define reusable rule groups for baseline protections and apply them consistently across Web ACLs. Use IaC and change control.

pci_dss.reason: Standardization supports change control and consistent implementation of security controls across environments.

items.title: WAF evidence collection is incomplete (cannot verify posture)
items.description: If AWS APIs required for WAF posture evaluation fail (permissions, throttling, unsupported operations), the audit cannot reliably conclude coverage or configuration status. This should be treated as an evidence-quality issue, not as a confirmed security misconfiguration.
items.remediation: Fix evidence collection errors first: ensure the audit principal has WAFv2 read permissions (wafv2:List*, wafv2:Get*, wafv2:ListResourcesForWebACL) and required service read permissions (CloudFront list distributions, ELBv2 describe load balancers, API Gateway/AppSync/Cognito list resources). Re-run the audit to obtain complete evidence.

pci_dss.reason: Security testing and verification processes require reliable evidence. Collection gaps undermine the ability to validate required controls.

items.title: Public API Gateway stages should be protected by AWS WAF
items.description: Public API Gateway endpoints are common internet entry points. Where APIs are in-scope for security/compliance, they should be protected by AWS WAF (REGIONAL) using Web ACL associations to stages.
items.remediation: Identify public REST/HTTP API stages and associate a WAFv2 Web ACL (REGIONAL). Start with AWS Managed Rules (CommonRuleSet/SQLi/BadInputs) and add rate-based rules tuned to expected traffic.

pci_dss.reason: Public-facing application endpoints must be protected by an automated technical solution that detects and prevents web-based attacks (e.g., WAF).

items.title: AppSync GraphQL APIs should be protected by AWS WAF
items.description: If AppSync GraphQL APIs are public/in-scope, they should be protected by WAF (REGIONAL). Lack of WAF increases exposure to common API and web-layer attacks.
items.remediation: Associate a WAFv2 Web ACL (REGIONAL) to in-scope AppSync APIs. Enable logging/metrics and tune rules using Count mode before enforcing Block.

pci_dss.reason: WAF protections are required for in-scope public-facing application components, including API endpoints.

items.title: Cognito User Pools should be protected by AWS WAF when exposed publicly
items.description: Cognito User Pools used for public authentication endpoints can be protected by AWS WAF to mitigate abuse and credential attacks. If these endpoints are in-scope, ensure WAF association and rate-based protections.
items.remediation: Associate a WAFv2 Web ACL (REGIONAL) to in-scope Cognito User Pools, enable logging/metrics, and configure rate-based protections for sign-in/sign-up endpoints.

pci_dss.reason: Security controls should address common software attacks; protecting authentication endpoints is a critical part of that posture.

notes: Expanded WAF checklist: adds evidence-quality handling (WAF-013) and coverage for additional WAF-supported internet entry points (API Gateway, AppSync, Cognito).
